Package hadur2.core.policy

package hadur2.core.policy
Aggressive (S5): the policies that decide how close Hadur fights and how hard it shoots. Unhittable (S6): the policies that change the movement's flavour and shed work when a tick runs slow.
  • DistancePolicy: the target distance the surf and the orbit steer to. It starts where the opening puts it and moves a step a wave on the gap between the two rolling hit rates (DIST-1); the endgame pulls it in to finish (END-1).
  • PowerPolicy: full-power shots against a gun the profile rates T0 (POW-1), or while this battle shows we out-hit them by a wide, certain margin (POW-2).
  • Endgame: the finishing and ramming states (END-1, END-2), with EnemyGunHeat to tell whose gun is cooler.
  • HitWindow: the rolling hit rate over the last 100 outcomes that DIST-1, POW-2 and MOVE-2 read, bounded by construction (RES-2).
  • MoveFlavour: the flattener, then go-to surfing, then a band 100 px further out, each added when their hit rate on us certainly beats the profile's (MOVE-2).
  • TickBudget: the computation level, one deeper for the next tick after a slow tick (TIME-1) and for the rest of the round after each skipped turn (TIME-2).
  • RammerPolicy: a robot driving straight at us, seen from its own closing speed; full power (RAM-1) and the escape (RAM-2) while it charges.
  • MirrorDetector: a robot that drives to a reflection of our position, which reflection and how late (MIR-1).

Every input is an Estimate, a value with its margin, and a policy takes its aggressive setting only once the margin allows it; otherwise it keeps the conservative one (DIAL-1). The package sees evidence only (waves, shots, energies), never BotInput or BotEvent, so nothing here can depend on elapsed ticks or the round number (DIAL-2). Gun and movement never see this package: the core applies its decisions through their setters, as it does the opening book's.

Dependencies, enforced by ArchitectureTest: this package may use only itself, opponent memory (for Estimate and the tiers), physics and the JDK. No gun, movement, KNN, ledger, melee, physics, model, memory or adapt code may depend on it, and it may not use the posture gate. Like the whole core it uses no robocode.* class (CORE-1) and no randomness, threads, reflection, I/O or clock (RES-6). The package is one of the duel's, pinned by DuelIdentityTest.

    The distance Hadur tries to fight at (the artifact's distance controller). 1.20 held a fixed 650 px, which on an 800x600 field is a retreat: bullets take 33-45 ticks to arrive and our own gun's escape angle is at its widest.

    How a wave moved the target: IN a step on a certain lead of ours, OUT a step on their lead, or HOLD with no clear lead either way, no rates yet, or the target already at the bound it would move toward.

    MoveFlavour
    MOVE-2: when the enemy hits us more than its profile says it does, beyond the margin of error, the movement changes flavour at the next surfable wave.
    MoveFlavour.Step
    The flavours in the order they are added; each keeps the ones before it.
    PowerPolicy
    When to fire full power instead of the gun's own choice, and, separately, when to fire less than it chose because a kill is already certain.
    PowerPolicy.Lead
    What the lead-aware regime (POW-7 to POW-9) asks of the gun's power: OFF leaves 1.20's choice, CHAFF is the minimum power, DEFAULT is the gun's base power without its power-down.
    PowerPolicy.Reason
    Why a shot got the power it did: GUN when no rule applies and the gun's own power stands, POW_1/POW_2/POW_3 for the full-power rules, POW_4 when the expected-value comparison picked full power over the gun's own.
    RammerPolicy
    RAM-1, RAM-2: recognising a robot that is simply driving at us, and the response to it, no profile or gun tier needed.
    TickBudget
    The tick budget (TIME-1, TIME-2): how much work the core may do this tick, as a computation level from 0 (everything) to TickBudget.MAX_LEVEL.
